The radar cross section (RCS) measurements were performed in two fully polarimetric compact radar ranges operating at 100 GHz and 240 GHz.
The root mean square (RMS) roughness values ranged from 96 microns for the unbrushed concrete to 201 microns for the sand.
The correlation length values ranged from 437 microns for the asphalt shingles to 799 microns for the unbrushed concrete.
The roughness parameter ks ranged from 0.2 to 1.012 across the different materials and frequencies.
The backscattering coefficient σ0 was independent of azimuth angle for all materials except the asphalt shingles.
The initial moisture content of the moist soil samples ranged from 0.14 g/cm3 to 0.23 g/cm3, which decreased to 0.05 g/cm3 to 0.10 g/cm3 by the end of the measurements.
The density of the dry soil was measured to be 1.19 g/cm3, while the sand had a density of 1.68 g/cm3.
The copolarization ratio σ0_HH/σ0_VV approached unity as the roughness parameter ks increased for the concrete samples.
The backscattering coefficient of the moist soil was lower than the dry soil, likely due to increased volumetric scattering effects in the dry soil.
The asphalt shingles showed an azimuthal dependence in their backscattering coefficient due to the organized pattern of the overlapping shingles, especially at lower elevation angles.
The backscattering coefficient was on average about 2 dB higher at 240 GHz compared to 100 GHz across the materials studied.
A stylus profilometer was used to measure the surface roughness of the concrete, shingles, and brushed surfaces, while an optical profilometer was used for the sand and soil samples.
The gravel surface roughness could not be accurately measured due to the large variations in the gravel's surface height.
The soil particle size distribution analysis showed that 96% of the sample mass contained particulates larger than 45 microns.
The average diameter of the gravel aggregates used in the study was approximately 10 mm.
